narrative:
The model estimates there’s a 26% chance you won’t pass your final year, which is above the 10% threshold that requires extra support. Because of this, you’ll need to take remedial courses to help you stay on track.

The main reasons the model is concerned come down to three key areas. First, your father’s education level stands out—most students who don’t need remedial courses have fathers with at least some secondary or higher education, while yours completed only primary school. This factor slightly increases the risk of struggling in your final year. On the positive side, you’ve never failed a class before, which works strongly in your favor. Additionally, your clear goal of pursuing higher education also helps reduce the predicted risk.

While these are the most influential factors, other details in your profile also played a role. For example, you study less than two hours a week, which is below what most students who pass their final year report. You also have a high number of school absences—22 compared to an average of just under 3—which raises concerns about consistency in your learning.

The remedial courses are an opportunity to strengthen your study habits, catch up on missed material, and build confidence. Focus on making the most of this support, especially by increasing your study time and reducing absences. With effort, you can improve your chances of success.
